description: Establish a clean baseline and scaffold the tools/muntutils/ directory. Confirm the existing tools build chain works before adding anything, create the feature branch, and lay down the tools/muntutils/ directory that later features fill in. This gates the rest of the work: if the baseline is not green we must know before building on it.
steps: From /projects/sandbox/udbr, create and switch to a feature branch: `git checkout -b feat/muntutils-source-trimmer-sizer` (if it already exists, check it out).

KNOWN PRE-EXISTING BASELINE ISSUE (confirmed, out of scope): `make -C tools all` fails on a pre-existing bug in the UNRELATED tool tools/pcopy/pcopy.c line 62 (`#define PCOPY_IOCTL_MAGIC 0xPC`, an invalid C integer literal that GCC 11.5.0 rejects). This is present verbatim in committed HEAD/pristine main (verified: `git diff HEAD -- tools/pcopy/` empty; `git show HEAD:tools/pcopy/pcopy.c` shows the same literal) and is NOT caused by this task. Do NOT modify pcopy/pmove: fixing unrelated committed source is outside this task's scope and was not authorized. muntutils is independent of pcopy/pmove. Baseline confidence comes instead from: system gcc/g++ 11.5.0 present and working, and `make -C tools clean` succeeding (exit 0). muntutils will be built and verified via its own build.sh and a targeted `make -C tools muntutils` target rather than the aggregate `all`.

Verify system toolchain: `gcc --version` and `g++ --version` should both report GCC 11.5.0. Confirm the derived GCC candidates under tools/gcc/build and tools/gcc/gcc-16.2.0/build are NOT present (so build.sh will fall back to system gcc/g++ and print the standard no -fme-metadata warning).
Create the directory tools/muntutils/ (empty placeholder is fine; later features add sources). Do not create any files that would break `make -C tools`.
Do NOT yet wire muntutils into tools/Makefile (that happens in FEAT-003 after sources exist) so the baseline chain stays green throughout.
acceptance_criteria: A feature branch feat/muntutils-source-trimmer-sizer exists and is checked out.
System toolchain confirmed: gcc and g++ both present (GCC 11.5.0). `make -C tools clean` succeeds (exit 0).

Pre-existing unrelated pcopy.c build breakage is documented as out of scope and NOT modified; muntutils build/verification uses its own build.sh and a targeted `make -C tools muntutils` target instead of the aggregate `all`.
`git status` shows only the intended new/untracked files under tools/muntutils/ and .agents/ (no unrelated modifications).
verification: Run `make -C tools clean` and confirm exit code 0.
Run `gcc --version` and `g++ --version` and confirm both are present.
Confirm the pre-existing pcopy.c `0xPC` breakage exists in committed HEAD (git show) so it is documented as pre-existing and unrelated.
findings:
Completed all actionable FEAT-001 steps except the baseline build gate (blocked by a pre-existing, out-of-scope pcopy.c bug):
- Branch: created and checked out `feat/muntutils-source-trimmer-sizer` (from main at 21a7d929b5).
- Toolchain verified: `gcc --version` and `g++ --version` both report GCC 11.5.0 (Red Hat 11.5.0-5).
- Derived GCC confirmed ABSENT: tools/gcc/build/gcc and tools/gcc/gcc-16.2.0/build/gcc do not exist, so build.sh will fall back to system gcc/g++ and print the standard no -fme-metadata warning as expected.
- Directory tools/muntutils/ created (empty placeholder; later features add sources). Note: git does not track empty directories, so it does not appear in `git status` yet; it exists on disk. A .gitkeep is intentionally NOT added to avoid pre-empting FEAT-002/FEAT-003 file layout, but can be added if the orchestrator wants the dir tracked before sources land.
- tools/Makefile NOT modified (deferred to FEAT-003), as instructed.
- `make -C tools clean` succeeds (exit 0).
- `make -C tools all` FAILS (exit 2) on the pre-existing pcopy.c:62 `0xPC` invalid-literal bug described in blocked_reason. This is the acceptance-criterion #2 gate and is why the feature is blocked.
- Tree state: only untracked .agents/ task dirs present; no unrelated modifications introduced by this work.
